compiled_state.description:
The Bedrock daily spend cap denies all Bedrock invocation while real spend is
near zero, because its empirical rate table is inflated by a factor of
1,000,000 for every marketplace-billed model.

Cost Explorer meters the two services Bedrock bills through in DIFFERENT units.
The legacy `Amazon Bedrock` service reports UsageQuantity in units of 1,000
tokens. The marketplace `... (Amazon Bedrock Edition)` services report it in
units of 1,000,000 tokens. `_refresh_rates` divided the marketplace quantity by
1,000 where it needed to multiply, so the derived rate landed 1,000,000x high.

Measured on this account, 2026-09-21, Claude Sonnet 4.6 input tokens:
UnblendedCost $11.1250 over UsageQuantity 3.3712 = $3.30 per unit, which is the
per-MILLION-token list price. The stored rate was 3300.0 "per 1,000 tokens".

Consequence: THRESHOLD_USD=500 is crossed after roughly 152,000 tokens. The
lambda attached BedrockDailySpendCapDeny to the Admin group 51 times in one
night, every time with $0.00 of real Cost Explorer spend for that day, blocking
a 252-cell review campaign. Actual Bedrock spend over the same period: $85.64 on
2026-09-21 and $0 after.

Both existing marketplace tests passed throughout, because each asserted the
implementation's own arithmetic (`cost / (quantity / 1000)`) rather than a known
price.
compiled_state.title: Bedrock spend cap rate table is 1,000,000x high for marketplace models
